principle: Academic groups are persistent institutional/shared-context structures over real Academy population slots. Group co-membership is not itself a social relationship.
rules: Academic grouping consumes existing cadet slots; it never creates cadets.
Latent and materialized cadets may belong to the same group.
Materialization preserves membership because membership is anchored to population_slot_ref.
A current class section may contain cadets from only one cadet class.
One cadet has exactly one primary class-section membership for the relevant grouping period.
Study groups require an academic context and do not create friendship, trust, affection or rivalry automatically.
Practical teams require actual course/activity eligibility.
Practical composition may use specialization/branch state where academically relevant but not species or personality as a balancing shortcut.
Player presence, dialogue initiation or narrative convenience cannot reshuffle groups.
Group reassignment requires an explicit academic/reorganization event and preserves prior membership history.
Group membership may provide future shared-context provenance for social events, but Step 3 does not mutate relationship state.
Roommates, schedules, social relationships and romance remain outside Step 3.
